sentences.text: The husband and wife were before the Family Court at Bengaluru in MC No.996 of 2017 and have settled the dispute amongst themselves by drawing up a memorandum of settlement.
The settlement also records and recognizes the closure of present proceedings.

The narration in the settlement, insofar as it concerns the present case, is as follows:
"5.

The petitioner/mother filed one police complaint against the respondent/father and his family members under Section 498A of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of DP Act,
which is numbered as C No.56339 of 2017 pending before the X Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Mayo Hall, Bengaluru.

entities.text: X Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Mayo Hall, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Both the parties undertake to co-operate in closing/withdrawing/ quashing the said case as per the law before the concern authority as and when required.

6. The petitioner/mother has filed Private Complaint against P. Ragavanka and Ashwathnarayanareddy N.V. under section 415, 416, 417, 418, 419, 420, 403, 406,
409. 463, 465, 467, 468, 469, 470, 120B r/w 34 of IPC on the file of III ACMM at Bengaluru and which is registered as CC No.3291 of 2018 and pending for consideration."

3. Again at paragraph 9 of the memorandum of settlement, it is narrated as under:
"The petitioner/Mother has agreed to withdraw or assist to close the above mentioned criminal cases filed by her against respondent/Father i.e. case No.CC NO.56339 of 2017 and CC No.3291 of 2018.

The petitioner has also agreed to close the above cases by appearing and submitting no objection in Criminal petitions 5405 of 2020 filed by respondent/Father with respect to quashing of the abovesaid criminal cases CC No.3921 of 2018 in view of the facts that the dispute has been settled amicably."

4. In the light of the settlement arrived at between the parties which also recognizes closure of the present case as a condition precedent, I deem it appropriate to accept the settlement, as the offences are ones punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code and under Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and are not against the State.

Therefore, for the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER 1. *Criminal Petition disposed of.
